title: DENSE-BAVARIA: AI-transformed dual early detection of breast cancer and diseases of the central cardiovascular system
summary:
Women between the ages of 50 and 75 in Germany can participate in regular mammography screening for the early detection of breast cancer. However, some women have very dense breast tissue. In such cases, conventional X-ray mammography is less effective at detecting changes or tumours. At the same time, women with dense breast tissue have a higher risk of developing breast cancer.

This study investigates how well a special form of AI-assisted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) without contrast agents can detect breast cancer in these women when mammography has previously been inconclusive. 

In addition to the accuracy of cancer detection, the study also records the acceptance and impact of the examination on the participants' quality of life. It also examines whether the data recorded can be used to detect other health-related changes, for example in large blood vessels such as the aorta.

interventions.name: Women with (very) high breast density who have a negative mammography screening result. The women receive a native MRI investigation after the X-ray screening mammography.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Mammographically dense or very dense breast, negative mammography screening result
Exclusion criteria:
MRI contraindications, pregnant or lactating women, claustrophobia, adiposity (> 150 kg)
